name: Track and release holdback
summary: Owners keep back 10% of every progress payment as holdback, and the contractor keeps back the same from its subcontractors, until the lien period after substantial performance has passed. This process releases that money: the project accountant reconciles owner and trade holdback, collects trade declarations and WSIB clearances, waits out the 60-day lien period, searches for liens, bills the owner and pays each trade. It is slow because of the statutory wait, liens that must be vacated, owners that hold payment for closeout documents and clearances that expire while waiting.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian national general contractor with about 220 active projects and about 10 projects reaching substantial performance each month, with holdback tracked in the ERP and Excel ledgers.
baseline.notes: Annual and phased release became possible in Ontario for contracts entered after 1 July 2018 when the contract provided for it; most 2019-2022 projects still released holdback once at substantial performance, with some early releases for trades that finished early.

unit_of_work: one holdback release (one project's substantial performance, or one phased or early trade release)
trigger: The consultant certifies substantial performance (or a phase or a subcontract is certified complete).
end_state: The owner has paid the holdback, each trade has been paid its holdback net of set-offs, and the ledger is closed.

volume.seasonality: More substantial performances in August (schools before the school year) and in November to December (projects pushed to completion before year end).

surge.cause: school and year-end projects reaching substantial performance together

evidence.note: School projects timed to September occupancy and year-end completions are the author's estimate.

About 10 substantial performances a month (organisation file: 7-14 deficiency closeouts and about 10 project starts a month) plus about 6 phased or early trade releases; lower than the organisation file's 15-40.

steps.name: Log the certificate and holdback dates
steps.description: The project accountant receives the certificate of substantial performance (or the subcontract completion or phased release notice) from the project team, records the certificate date in the holdback ledger and diarises the end of the 60-day lien period and the expected owner payment date.

error.defect_description: Lien period diarised from the wrong date.

evidence.note: 60-day lien preservation period from the trigger date.

steps.name: Confirm the certificate has been published
steps.description: The project accountant checks the construction trade newspaper listing or the consultant's confirmation that the certificate was published, because the lien and holdback periods run from publication, and asks the consultant or owner to publish if not.

control.basis: Ontario Construction Act s. 32: publication of the certificate of substantial performance starts the lien period

evidence.note: Publication as the start of the lien period is from the author's knowledge of the Act; the opened sources give the 60-day period but not the publication rule.

steps.name: Reconcile owner and subcontractor holdback
steps.description: The project accountant compares holdback retained by the owner on every certified draw with holdback the company retained from each subcontractor in AP, trade by trade, and resolves differences caused by credits, change orders and earlier partial releases.

error.defect_description: A subcontract's holdback is understated after a change order credit.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the organisation file shows the holdback ledger coming from subcontractor payment.

steps.name: Confirm final subcontract values and set-offs
steps.description: The project manager reviews each trade's final subcontract value, open deficiencies and backcharges, and decides which trades' holdback can be released in full and where an amount must be kept back as set-off for unfinished or defective work.

error.defect_description: A backcharge is forgotten and the full holdback is paid.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Prepare the holdback invoice to the owner
steps.description: The billing specialist drafts the holdback invoice to the owner for the total holdback retained, attaches a statutory declaration and a current WSIB clearance, and holds it ready to submit once the lien period ends.

error.defect_description: Holdback total does not match the owner's records.

control.basis: CCDC 2 GC 5.2 / 5.4: statutory declaration and workers' compensation evidence with the holdback application

evidence.note: Declaration and workers' compensation evidence with applications; clearance valid up to 90 days.

steps.name: Collect trade declarations and clearances
steps.description: The project accountant emails each of the 15 to 30 subcontractors for a statutory declaration that their own trades and suppliers are paid and a current WSIB clearance, logs what arrives, and chases the missing ones by phone.

error.defect_description: A declaration from a sub-subcontracting trade is missing or stale.

control.basis: WSIB clearance policy 14-02-19: principal liable for a contractor's unpaid premiums without a valid clearance

evidence.note: Principal liability without a clearance; number of trades is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for the lien period to expire
steps.description: Holdback cannot be paid until the 60-day lien period after publication has passed; the documents gathered so far wait for the remainder of that period, while the owner may publish a notice refusing part of the holdback.

next.condition: owner publishes a notice of non-payment of holdback

evidence.note: 60-day lien period and mandatory release unless the payer publishes a notice of non-payment of holdback. The wait here is the part of the 60 days left after steps s02-s06, which run inside the period. Share with a notice is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Negotiate the owner's withheld holdback
steps.description: The project manager reviews the owner's notice of non-payment of holdback, usually for deficiencies or claimed delay, agrees a reduced set-off or a plan to complete the work, and refers unresolved amounts to legal for adjudication.

evidence.note: Owner may refuse holdback only by publishing a notice.

steps.name: Search for registered and served liens
steps.description: The project accountant orders a title search through the land registry for private projects, or checks with the owner for written notices of lien on public projects where liens cannot be registered, and checks legal's register of liens and claims.

control.basis: Construction Act: no holdback paid while a lien is preserved; lien search before release

next.condition: lien preserved by a trade or supplier

evidence.note: Lien share is the author's estimate; the land registry portal is the government portal system in the organisation file.

steps.name: Arrange to vacate the lien
steps.description: Contracts counsel reviews the lien, asks the trade to discharge it if the claim is paid or wrong, or arranges a bond or cash security to vacate it from title by court order so the rest of the holdback can be released.

evidence.note: Holdback security by letter of credit or bond; lien handling time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for the lien to be discharged or vacated
steps.description: The trade discharges the lien after payment or settlement, or the court vacates it on posting of security; the release waits for written confirmation on title or from the owner.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Submit the holdback invoice
steps.description: The billing specialist dates and submits the holdback invoice with the declaration, clearance and lien search to the consultant and the owner, and logs it in the collections tracker with the contract's payment date.

steps.name: Wait for the owner to pay the holdback
steps.description: The consultant certifies the holdback payment and the owner processes it; CCDC 2-2020 requires payment within 10 working days after the holdback period, but owners often pay later while closeout documents are still being reviewed.

next.condition: not paid by the due date

evidence.note: 10 working days after the holdback period under CCDC 2-2020; late share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Chase the owner for holdback
steps.description: The billing specialist chases the owner's accounts payable and the consultant, finds out what is holding the payment, such as missing as-built drawings or manuals, and asks the project team to deliver it.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Apply the holdback receipt
steps.description: The billing specialist matches the owner's holdback payment to the holdback invoice in the ERP and tells the project accountant that trade holdback can now be paid.

error.defect_description: Receipt applied to progress billings instead of holdback.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Prepare the trade holdback payment list
steps.description: The project accountant builds the list of trade holdback payments net of set-offs and backcharges and checks for each trade that the statutory declaration is on file and the WSIB clearance is still within its validity period on the payment date.

error.defect_description: Wrong set-off applied to a trade.

control.basis: WSIB clearance policy 14-02-19: valid clearance for each contractor at the time of payment

next.condition: a clearance has expired or a declaration is missing

evidence.note: Clearance validity up to 90 days, so documents gathered before the lien period often expire.

steps.name: Refresh expired clearances and declarations
steps.description: The project accountant asks the trades with expired WSIB clearances or missing declarations for new ones, downloads clearances from the WSIB portal where possible, and adds them to the file.

steps.name: Project manager approves trade releases
steps.description: The project manager checks the payment list against the release list and the owner's payment, confirms that set-offs are kept back for unfinished work, and approves the trade holdback releases in the AP workflow.

control.basis: Project manager approval of subcontract payments separate from the accountant who prepares them

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Finance manager approves the payment run
steps.description: The regional finance manager reviews the holdback payment batch, checks the total against holdback received from the owner, and releases it under signing authority for the next AP payment run.

control.basis: Signing authority: finance manager release of payment batches above project limits

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the finance manager is not listed on this process in the organisation file.

steps.name: Pay trade holdback in the AP run
steps.description: The ERP includes the released holdback payments in the next scheduled AP payment run and sends EFT payments or prints cheques to each subcontractor without further handling.

evidence.note: Weekly AP runs; the Act's payment periods down the chain set the outer limit (author's reading). Run frequency is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Close out the holdback ledger
steps.description: The project accountant clears the holdback receivable and payable in the ERP, records any holdback kept back for set-offs, files the release documents and marks the project's holdback as released.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Lien preserved by a trade or supplier
exceptions.description: Legal arranges discharge or vacates the lien with security before the holdback is paid.

exceptions.name: Owner notice of non-payment of holdback
exceptions.description: The owner publishes a notice keeping part of the holdback for deficiencies; the PM negotiates the set-off.

exceptions.name: Owner pays holdback late
exceptions.description: The owner holds payment, often for closeout documents, and the billing specialist chases.

exceptions.name: Expired trade clearances
exceptions.description: Clearances gathered before the lien period expire before payment and must be refreshed.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from substantial performance certificate to trade holdback paid
benchmarks.population: Holdback releases on Canadian building projects, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author's estimate built on the statutory floor below plus publication, owner payment and AP run delays.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from publication to latest CCDC owner payment date (60-day lien period + 10 working days)

evidence.note: 60-day lien preservation period and 10 working days after the holdback period; sum by the author.

pain_points.description: The 60-day lien period is fixed by law, so most of the cycle is waiting.
Collecting declarations and clearances from every trade is manual chasing, and clearances valid for at most 90 days often expire before payment.
Owners hold holdback until closeout documents arrive even after the lien period, and liens must be vacated before release.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

assumptions: Loaded costs come from the organisation file (1.35 loading on salaried wages).
Steps s02 to s06 run inside the 60-day lien period, so s07 holds only the remainder (30 to 46 days).

The finance manager and contracts counsel are added because the payment batch and lien vacating need them; the organisation file lists only the project accountant, billing specialist and project manager on this process.
Volume is set at 10-24 a month (mode 16), below the organisation file's 15-40, because substantial performances run at about 10 a month; early trade and phased releases are counted as separate cases.
Early releases for trades certified complete (35% of cases) follow the same steps with a smaller trade list.

The simulated median cycle time (94.9 days) matches the 95-day estimate; the simulated p90 (121 days) is shorter than the 140-day estimate because long lien disputes and owners holding holdback for months are rarer than a triangular range can show. Stated FTEs (1.8) match touch time x volume.

sources.title: Prompt Payment for Construction in Ontario
sources.supports: Construction Act Part I.1 in force 1 October 2019 for contracts entered after that date; proper invoice monthly unless the contract says otherwise and cannot depend on certifier action; owner pays within 28 days; owner notice of non-payment within 14 days; contractor pays subcontractors within 7 days of receiving payment, or 35 days after the proper invoice unless it gives notice; undertaking to adjudicate within 21 days.

sources.title: Prompt payment and adjudication have arrived in Ontario
sources.supports: Holdback release mandatory unless the payer publishes a notice of non-payment of holdback; annual or phased release allowed with contract provisions; holdback may be secured by letter of credit or bond; lien preservation 60 days and perfection 90 days; adjudicator decision within 30 days; payment within 10 days of a determination.

sources.title: The new CCDC 2 - 2020: contract changes you need to know
sources.supports: Monthly applications for payment to the consultant and owner simultaneously; workers' compensation evidence and a CCDC 9A statutory declaration with each application after the first; owner pays within 28 days (20 days under CCDC 2-2008); holdback paid no later than 10 working days after the holdback period expires; consultant responds to a Ready-for-Takeover application within 10 days.

sources.title: Clearance Certificate in Construction (Operational Policy Manual document 14-02-19)
sources.supports: A principal that retains a construction contractor must have a clearance in place for the whole time the contractor works; a clearance is valid for up to 90 calendar days and is renewable; without one the principal may be liable for the contractor's WSIB obligations up to the labour portion of the contract; records kept 3 years; policy applies from 1 January 2020.
